subject: Patch window, escalation play & CVE triage attestation for SIG questionnaire
messages:
From: Priya Menon <priya.menon@acme-corp.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, Kenji Tanaka <kenji@skynet.io>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 15:03:00 -0400
Subject: SIG follow-up: request for patch cadence, escalation play and attestation

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the demo last week — Acme's InfoSec team is working through the SIG/CAIQ and we need a concise set of artifacts related to vulnerability management for our vendor assessment. Specifically we are requesting: 

- A short description of scan cadence (authenticated vs unauthenticated), scope, and how false positives are handled.
- SLA commitments for CVE remediation by severity and the escalation/playbook we follow for critical/actively exploited CVEs.
- A signed attestation we can include in the SIG answers (one paragraph + point-form SLA table is fine).
- Any evidence artifacts (scan summary, example remediation ticket, or a simple matrix that maps patch windows to environments).

Can you confirm whether these apply to both Hosted API and Dedicated customers, and whether Private (VPC/on-prem) customers follow the same cadence or require customer coordination?

We are on a tight timeline for our SIG submission — would you be able to get these to us by end of day Wednesday, 14 July?

Appreciate it,

Priya Menon
Senior Security Manager, Acme Cloud Services
security@acme-corp.com

Attachments: none

From: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
To: Priya Menon <priya.menon@acme-corp.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, Kenji Tanaka <kenji@skynet.io>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 18:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: request for patch cadence, escalation play and attestation

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear list. We can provide everything you requested. High-level summary below; I’m attaching a compact patch-window matrix and a one-page scan-summary for context. I’ll follow up with a signed attestation that you can paste into the SIG answers.

Quick answers:
- Scan cadence and scope:
  - Authenticated full-stack scans: weekly, covering control plane + core inference services (nightly vulnerability quick-scan for critical CVEs).
  - Unauthenticated external surface scans: nightly for critical/high checks, weekly full external pass.
  - False positives: triage pipeline uses asset fingerprinting + reproducible PoC requirement; items marked as FP are logged with rationale in Jira ticket and excluded from SLA calculations once agreed.

- CVE remediation SLAs (default, applied to Hosted API and Dedicated):
  - Critical (active exploit or root RCE): initial mitigation/temporary control within 24–48 hours, full remediation or rollback window within 72 hours when possible.
  - High (privilege escalation, remote code possibility): target remediation within 7 calendar days.
  - Medium: target remediation within 30 calendar days.
  - Low/Informational: tracked and remediated on regular maintenance cadence (target 90 days).

- Escalation & triage play:
  - Severity triage within 4 hours of detection for Critical, 24 hours for High.
  - On-call security (pager): security-oncall@redwood.ai / PagerDuty (PD escalation path).
  - If a fix requires cross-functional change (infra, runtime, model ops), owner is assigned in the triage ticket and escalates to engineering manager + security if SLA at risk.

- Private (VPC/on-prem) customers:
  - Default: customer-managed patching. Redwood provides advisory guidance, reproducible PoCs, recommended patch artifacts, and optional managed-support arrangement under contract (managed patching modifies SLAs; we’ll state specifics in contract amendment).

I attached: patch_window_matrix.xlsx (matrix mapping environment, maintenance windows, and expected downtime), scan_report_summary.pdf (example sanitized scan summary). Also attached a sample repro for a recent CVE we patched (cve-2027-1144-repro.txt) to show our ticketing and remediation notes.

We can deliver a signed attestation by Wednesday EOD; looping in Marcus and Laura for visibility.

Best,

Aditya Rao
Director, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0131

Attachments: patch_window_matrix.xlsx, scan_report_summary.pdf, cve-2027-1144-repro.txt

From: Priya Menon <priya.menon@acme-corp.com>

Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, Kenji Tanaka <kenji@skynet.io>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 09:47:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: request for patch cadence, escalation play and attestation

Thanks — this is very helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we include the attestation in the SIG answers:

1) When you say "initial mitigation within 24–48 hours" for Critical, can you confirm whether that could be a configuration rollback or a WAF rule while a full patch is worked on?
2) For Dedicated customers, are the same SLAs contractual by default or are they dependent on a dedicated plan (i.e., do we need a committed capacity contract to include 72-hour remediation)?

Also — for the attestation we need a small paragraph (one or two sentences) we can paste, plus a signed name/title and date. Example (not exact): "Redwood Inference attests that it performs weekly authenticated scans, etc." If you can paste the exact verbiage you would like to sign off on that would be ideal.

Appreciate the attachments — I’ll circulate to our procurement team as well.

Best,
Priya

On Mon, Jul 12, 2027 at 6:22 PM aditya.rao@redwood.ai wrote:
> Hi Priya — thanks for the clear list...

From: aditya.rao@redwood.ai

Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, Kenji Tanaka <kenji@skynet.io>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: request for patch cadence, escalation play and attestation

Priya — thanks for the questions. Short answers: yes on mitigations, and Dedicated is covered by our standard Dedicated offering SLAs when a reserved capacity contract is in place. Private/VPC customers require coordination and a separate managed-support agreement if they need Redwood to perform patching under SLA.

Below is the attestation language you can paste into the SIG. I’m including a concise SLA table immediately after.

--- BEGIN ATTESTATION ---
Redwood Inference attests that, as part of its vulnerability management program, it performs weekly authenticated scans across core infrastructure and nightly quick-scans for critical findings; triages detected issues with a documented severity classification, and follows defined remediation SLAs. For Critical vulnerabilities with evidence of active exploitation, Redwood initiates mitigation controls (for example, configuration rollbacks or WAF rules) within 24–48 hours and works to fully remediate within 72 hours where feasible. For Dedicated customers with a reserved-capacity contract, the remediation SLAs described herein are enforceable as part of the contract; Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments require customer coordination or a managed-services amendment to receive equivalent patching SLAs.

Signed: Aditya Rao
Title: Director, Trust & Security, Redwood Inference
Date: 2027-07-14
--- END ATTESTATION ---

SLA table (for inclusion in SIG answer):
- Critical (active exploit): mitigation 24–48 hours; target full remediation 72 hours (exceptions documented).
- High: target remediation 7 calendar days.
- Medium: target remediation 30 calendar days.
- Low: scheduled remediation via maintenance (target 90 days).

Evidence provided (attachments): patch_window_matrix.xlsx — maintenance/patch window mapping; scan_report_summary.pdf — sanitized scan summary for a recent assessment; cve-2027-1144-repro.txt — example repro and remediation note (sanitized).

If you need the attestation on company letterhead or a DocuSign signature, let me know and I’ll coordinate with Legal.

Regards,

Aditya Rao
Director, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference
